Level 0 asks for static files only — no engine — namely exported `content/<type-plural>/<slug>.md` items with `type`, `title` and `prov` frontmatter, a `content/index.md`, plus `/graph.jsonld`, `/llms.txt` and `/.well-known/knowledge-linkset` (a link set whose only top-level member is `linkset`, omitting every digest and `agsc-*` attribute). A Concept in a Bundle is a unit of knowledge in a Bundle, qualified by kind: pattern, taxonomy, explainer, principle, decision, spec, task, term or architecture; in the graph it is an `asc:Concept`, a subclass of `skos:Concept`, carrying `skos:inScheme` the Bundle, its title as `skos:prefLabel` and its description as `skos:definition`.

Sources: publish-a-level-0-node, concept

question_run: How does an item reference each entry in the graph?
answer:
An item references each entry in the graph by slug: a Link is a typed relation between two items of the same Bundle, written as a frontmatter array under one of fourteen keys (the nine core keys `related`, `broader`, `narrower`, `uses`, `requires`, `excludes`, `derived-from`, `contradicts`, `supersedes`, and the five Mode-2 keys `implements`, `verifies`, `covers`, `blocked-by`, `decided-by`), and each value is a slug. A Link never crosses Bundles, so a reference to another node is instead a citation in `sources[]`.
